headline: The index didn't move and the insides got shredded: a 52-week-high long bond is quietly liquidating anything with a factory, a mine or a mortgage attached.
summary: Yesterday was a dollar squeeze. Today the dollar stopped being the marginal story — DXY +0.4% to 102.25 is still pinned at the 100th percentile but the composite improved to -19, and bond vol finally broke lower, MOVE -2.5% on the day and -7.1% on the week to 102.56. None of that helped. SPX -0.2% and NDX -0.2% are cosmetic: underneath, CAT -5.7%, XLI -2.2%, XME -3.1%, COPX -3.1%, PAVE -2.5%, GRID -2.5%, ITA -2.2%, NLR -3.8%, URA -4.5%, REMX -3.0%. The pain rotated from FX into the physical economy.

The mechanism is the long end, and it is term premium, not growth. The 2-year fell 2bp today and 11bp on the week to 4.77%, while the 30-year rose 3bp to 5.67% — the 100th percentile of 52 weeks, acceleration z=1.08 — and the 10-year sits at 5.28%, 97.8th percentile, +50bp on the month. 2s10s has steepened 10bp on the month to 51bp. The 10-year real yield is 2.92% with z=1.92 and acceleration 1.38, 36% above its 200-day. The 30-year mortgage is 7.28%, +62bp on the month, at the 100th percentile. Rates composite -80, unchanged. A friendlier front end does not re-rate a long-duration equity market when the discount rate is being set 30 years out.

Breadth is now the single worst number on the board and it got worse: RSP/SPY -0.6% to z=-2.13 at the 0th percentile of 52 weeks, IWM/SPY -7.0% on the month at z=-1.95, RUT -1.3%, MDY -1.6%, while QQQ/SPY is at z=1.64 and the 84th percentile. Narrowness is the trade and it is extreme. What is holding is credit and cheap equity insurance: HYG/IEF at the 97.5th percentile and +1.0% on the month, BKLN at the 93rd, credit composite 42 — this is discount-rate pain, not default pain. But VIX 15.08 sits at the 9th percentile, VIX3M 17.72 at the 2.5th, SKEW -6.4% on the month with acceleration -1.85, against MOVE at z=2.19. Bond vol rich, equity vol at the bottom of its range, breadth at the bottom of its range. That asymmetry is the cleanest thing on the page.

The hard-asset unwind kept accelerating and it is monetary, not cyclical: gold -1.2% to 4,136 (-7.6% on the month, z=-1.83), silver -9.0% and platinum -9.8% on the month, GDX -3.1% with month acceleration -2.23, GDXJ -3.9%. Yet copper rose 0.8% and copper/gold is +9.0% on the month at the 100th percentile. Growth pulse 13. Crypto cracked a second day — BTC -2.6%, ETH -4.5%, SOL -3.7%, MSTR -6.8%, COIN -3.9% — the same long-duration-liquidity trade as small caps. EM continues to split by its currency: EWZ +13.7% on the week with USDBRL -2.8% on the month, versus INDA -7.6% on the month at the 7th percentile with USDINR z=1.47 and acceleration 1.59, EZA -13.1% and TUR -13.7%. Mega-cap quality took the flows — AMZN +1.4%, AAPL +0.9%, GOOGL +0.8%, LLY +2.7%, XLV +1.0% as the best sector.

good.text: Credit refuses to confirm any of the equity damage: HYG/IEF at the 97.5th percentile and +1.0% on the month, BKLN at the 93rd percentile, credit & vol composite 42. Spreads say discount rate, not default cycle.
Bond vol is finally coming in and the front end is rallying: MOVE -2.5% today, -7.1% on the week, 2-year -11bp on the week to 4.77%. The curve is steepening from the right end for once.

Inflation expectations stayed dead through the whole yield move: 5y breakeven 2.37 flat on the month and rolling over, 10y breakeven 2.36 (+1bp), RBOB -5.9% today and -10.4% on the week. The long-end selloff is not an inflation scare.

The growth signal inside commodities is still positive: copper +0.8% and copper/gold +2.0% to the 100th percentile of 52 weeks (+9.0% on the month, acceleration 1.45). This is a metals-as-money unwind, not a demand bust.

AI/compute leadership is intact on any horizon longer than a day: SOXX +12.2% and SMH +10.2% on the month, CIBR +12.7% at the 97th percentile, AMD +35.2%, MU +4.1% today, high-beta/low-vol at the 99th percentile.
Health care was the one sector that worked, up 1.0% with relative strength turning up, led by LLY +2.7% — a defensive that doesn't carry duration risk.

bad.text: The long bond made a new 52-week high in yield: 30y 5.67% (pos52 = 1.00, acceleration 1.08), 10y 5.28% at the 98th percentile, 10y real yield 2.92% with z=1.92. Rates composite -80.
Breadth broke to the worst reading on the board: RSP/SPY at the 0th percentile with z=-2.13 and acceleration -1.42, IWM/SPY -7.0% on the month, Russell -1.3%, midcaps -1.6%.

Today's liquidation was in real-economy cyclicals, and it accelerated: CAT -5.7%, DE -3.8%, XLI -2.2% (relative strength -10.8% over three months), XME -3.1%, COPX -3.1% even with copper up, REMX -3.0%, NLR -3.8%, URA -4.5%.

Housing is in outright recession pricing: 30-year mortgage 7.28% (+62bp on the month, 100th percentile), ITB -2.6% to the 0th percentile of 52 weeks, XHB -2.5%, DHI -2.5%, HD -11.0% on the month at the 4th percentile.

The dollar is still choking everything offshore even on a quieter day: EURUSD at the 0th percentile, USDMXN z=2.30 with acceleration 1.84, USDCAD z=1.89, USDINR z=1.47; EFA/SPY at the 0th percentile, EZA -2.2%, TUR -1.8%, GREK -3.1%.
Crypto's second straight crack confirms a liquidity drain, not a one-day shakeout: BTC -2.6%, ETH -4.5%, SOL -3.7%, MSTR -6.8%, COIN -3.9%, all with negative daily acceleration.

trades.name: 2s30s steepener via short TLT / long IEF
trades.line: Steepener: short TLT vs long IEF as the long end sets highs
trades.expr: Short TLT against a duration-matched IEF long (~2.2x IEF notional per TLT), or pay 30y / receive 2y in swaps. Options version: buy TLT Jan 75 puts funded by selling 82 calls.
trades.thesis: The Fed is being priced into the front end while term premium is being repriced at the back. 2y -11bp on the week versus 30y +3bp to a 52-week high is the signature of supply/term-premium, not growth — and it continues until the long end clears.
trades.trigger: 30y 5.67%, pos52 = 1.00, acceleration z=1.08; 10y 5.28% at the 98th percentile; 2s10s +10bp on the month to 51bp; MOVE -7.1% on the week means you can put this on with vol cheaper than a week ago.
trades.stop: 2s10s back below 40bp, or a 30y close under 5.45% on a genuine bull-flattening (front end selling off with the back end rallying).

trades.name: Short ITB (home construction)
trades.line: Short ITB: 7.28% mortgage, housing complex at 0th percentile
trades.expr: Short ITB outright, or ITB vs an equal-dollar SPY long. Higher-beta expression: DHI Jan puts.
trades.thesis: A 7.28% mortgage at the 100th percentile with the 10y real yield at z=1.92 is a direct cash-flow hit to builders, and the related tape is already confirming — HD, DHI and XHB all at the bottom of their 52-week ranges. There is no bounce without the long end.
trades.trigger: ITB -2.6% today, -9.0% on the month, 12% below its 200-day, pos52 = 0.00; XHB/SPY -8.6% on the month at the 0th percentile; mortgage +62bp on the month; HD -11.0% on the month at the 4.5th percentile.
trades.stop: 30-year mortgage back under 6.75%, or ITB reclaiming its 200-day (~+12% from here).

trades.name: Long QQQ / short IWM
trades.line: Own the narrowness: long QQQ, short IWM, dollar-neutral
trades.expr: Dollar-neutral long QQQ / short IWM. Alternative: long QQQ Dec calls vs short IWM Dec calls, same delta.
trades.thesis: Small caps are the highest-duration, most rate-sensitive, most domestically-levered part of the index, and the long end is still rising. Cash-rich mega-cap compute is the only place earning its multiple. Fight the narrowness later; it is still the trend.
trades.trigger: IWM -1.3% today; IWM/SPY -7.0% on the month at z=-1.95; RSP/SPY at the 0th percentile with z=-2.13; QQQ/SPY z=1.64 and trending up; SOXX +12.2% on the month.
trades.stop: IWM/SPY reclaiming its 200-day (6.8% above spot) or RSP/SPY turning up for two straight weeks — that is the regime change.

trades.name: Long equity tails (SPX put spreads / VIX3M)
trades.line: Buy cheap crash: VIX 9th pctile vs MOVE z=2.19
trades.expr: Buy 3-month SPX put spreads ~5% x 12% out of the money; or long VIX3M futures against a short front-VIX leg to avoid bleeding carry.
trades.thesis: Equity vol is priced for the index, which is flat; the internals are priced for a bear market. Bond vol is two standard deviations rich while equity tails keep getting cheaper. You are being paid to own the convexity that bond investors already own.
trades.trigger: VIX 15.08 at the 9th percentile and VIX3M 17.72 at the 2.5th; SKEW -6.4% on the month with acceleration -1.85; MOVE z=2.19; breadth at the 0th percentile with the 30y at a 52-week high in yield.
trades.stop: Defined-risk premium; kill it if SPX gains 3% with RSP/SPY turning up at the same time — that would be a genuine broadening, not a melt-up.

trades.name: Long EWZ / short INDA
trades.line: EM splits by FX: long Brazil, short India
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long EWZ / short INDA. Add a long BRL vs short INR forward overlay if you can run FX.
trades.thesis: The dollar is sorting EM by current account and carry. Brazil has a falling USDBRL, a 52-week-high index and the best relative strength on the board; India has a rising USDINR, an index at the 7th percentile and relentless outflows. Keep the pair, not the beta.
trades.trigger: EWZ +13.7% on the week, +11.9% on the month, relative strength +10.6%/+17.8%; BVSP z=1.74; USDBRL -2.8% on the month. Against it INDA -7.6% on the month at the 7th percentile with USDINR z=1.47 and acceleration 1.59.
trades.stop: USDBRL turning back up through 5.15, or EWZ losing 40 (below its 200-day region).

trades.name: Long XLV / short XLI
trades.line: Long health care, short industrials: defensives w/o duration
trades.expr: Equal-dollar long XLV / short XLI. Concentrated version: long LLY, short CAT.
trades.thesis: Industrials carry capex, backlog and rate sensitivity into a 5.67% 30-year; today's tape confirmed the unwind has started in the biggest names. Health care gives you defense without the bond proxy problem that is killing utilities and REITs.
trades.trigger: XLV +1.0%, the only green sector, relative strength turning up; XLI -2.2% with relative strength -5.1%/-10.8% and rolling over; CAT -5.7%, DE -3.8%, ETN -3.1%, PAVE -2.5% all in one session; XLU -3.8% and XLRE -6.9% on the month rule out the usual defensives.
trades.stop: Pair drawdown of 4%, or XLI relative strength turning back up with the 30y below 5.45%.
trades.target: +8% on the pair over a quarter.

trades.name: Long VST (gas-fired power) / short URA
trades.line: Long VST vs short uranium: electrons now, fuel stories later
trades.expr: Long VST (add CEG for diversification) against a short URA leg of equal dollars.
trades.thesis: The power-demand trade is bifurcating: cash-generating merchant generators are being bid while the speculative fuel-cycle names are being liquidated with the rest of the high-duration complex. Own the cash flows, short the story.
trades.trigger: VST +3.9% today and +20.5% on the week, CEG +17.9% on the week, natural gas +4.8% today and +9.7% on the month and turning up — against URA -4.5% today (-13.3% on the month, 10th percentile) and NLR -3.8% (-12.2% on the month, 4th percentile).
trades.stop: Natural gas back below 2.95, or VST giving back the week's 20% move; pair stop at -8%.
